# Storage and EV Battery Fleet (BatteryFleetAdapter)

> **Class**: `energysim.container.BatteryFleetAdapter` | add to a world with `add_fleet(fleet_type='battery', ...)` (accepted kinds: `battery`, `battery_fleet`, `ev`)

## Overview

High-performance vectorized battery energy storage / EV fleet adapter.

Simulates N battery units simultaneously using pure NumPy vector operations:

  - State of Charge (SoC) tracking: dSoC/dt = P * eta / Capacity (charging),
    P / eta / Capacity (discharging); ``P > 0`` charges, ``P < 0`` discharges (AC side)
  - Per-unit capacity and power limits
  - Charge / discharge efficiency (same ``efficiency`` each way)
  - Automatic power clipping when full or empty
  - ``loss_kw``: conversion loss power, so that per step
    ``P_ac * dt - d(stored energy) == loss_kw * dt`` exactly (energy conservation).

A SoC outside ``[soc_min, soc_max]`` at the start (e.g. set by the user) is clamped into
that range at the next step; energy conservation holds for in-range states. A step with
``step_size <= 0`` is a no-op.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | `'battery_fleet'` | - | Container (simulator) name. |
| `size` | `int` | `100` | - | Number of entities N in the fleet. |
| `capacity_kwh` | `Union[float, np.ndarray]` | `50.0` | kWh | Nominal storage capacity (scalar or length-N array). |
| `max_charge_kw` | `Union[float, np.ndarray]` | `11.0` | kW | Maximum charge power (AC side). |
| `max_discharge_kw` | `Union[float, np.ndarray]` | `11.0` | kW | Maximum discharge power (AC side). |
| `initial_soc` | `Union[float, np.ndarray]` | `0.5` | 1 | Initial state of charge. |
| `soc_min` | `float` | `0.05` | 1 | Lower SoC bound. |
| `soc_max` | `float` | `0.95` | 1 | Upper SoC bound. |
| `efficiency` | `float` | `0.95` | 1 | One-way conversion efficiency (charge and discharge). |
| `step_size` | `float` | `900.0` | s | Micro time-step. |

## Inputs

| Variable | Unit | Aliases |
|---|---|---|
| `p_cmd_kw` | kW | `p_cmd`, `p_req` |

## Outputs

| Variable | Unit | Aliases |
|---|---|---|
| `soc` | 1 | - |
| `actual_p_kw` | kW | `power`, `p_kw`, `actual_p` |
| `loss_kw` | kW | `losses_kw` |

Every output `<var>` is also available as `total_<var>`, `mean_<var>`, `min_<var>`, `max_<var>` and per entity as `<var>[i]`. Units that read `unspecified` are not declared by the container; connections to or from them are never rescaled (see [Units](../units.md)).

## Validation

The fleet is tested against an explicit loop of scalar models (`tests/strengths/test_vectorized_fleets.py`); see [Validation](../validation.md).

## Usage example

```python
from energysim import world

sim = world(start_time=0, stop_time=3600, t_macro=900, power_unit='kW')
sim.add_fleet(fleet_type='battery', name='ev_fleet', size=100, capacity_kwh=50.0,
              max_charge_kw=11.0, initial_soc=0.2, step_size=900, power_unit='kW')
sim.add_signal('charge_dispatch', lambda t: [7.4], step_size=900, power_unit='kW')
sim.add_connections({'charge_dispatch.y': 'ev_fleet.p_cmd'})   # scalar broadcast to all 100 units
res = sim.simulate()
print(res['ev_fleet.mean_soc'])
```
